title: implement subnet-claim leasing + conditional privatelink proxy for control-plane handoffs
author: Sofia Chen
release_notes: Adds a subnet-claim leasing mechanism and an optional Privatelink proxy component to improve zonal control plane failover. Backwards-compatible; new flags are opt-in. Includes Terraform module changes and Helm chart values for the proxy. See upgrade notes for rollback steps.
description:
Motivation: customers running Private control planes across multi-AZ VPCs need a deterministic, contest-free way to claim and release ephemeral control-plane subnets during scale-up, failover and upgrade operations. This PR introduces a lease-based subnet-claim mechanism (Terraform + installer runtime) and an optional conditional Privatelink proxy that allows control plane endpoints to remain reachable when route handoffs are staged across AZs.

What this change does: - New Terraform module: subnet-claiming that creates a DynamoDB-style lease record (implemented as a stateful lock backed by S3+state & tags) and exposes outputs for claimed-subnet-id and claim-expiry. - Installer runtime: controller that queries the lease endpoint and drains / attaches controlplane ENIs with a jittered backoff to avoid thundering-herd. - Privatelink proxy: Helm chart that deploys an AZ-aware envoy sidecar-ish proxy in customer VPCs (optional via values) to provide staged DNS/privatelink handoff without full TF-driven SG swaps. - DNS handoff hooks: staged Route53 record updates with TTL-lowering, health-check gating and an automatic rollback window. - Upgrade/rollback tooling: a new `installer rollback-subnet-claim` command plus idempotent reconciler for partial failure cases.

Files & surface area (high-level): - terraform/modules/subnet-claim/ main.tf, outputs.tf, README.md - helm/privatelink-proxy/ Chart.yaml, values.schema.json, templates/deployment.yaml - installer/cmd/lease-manager: new CLI + systemd unit (for on-prem) - installer/upgrade: rollback helpers and upgrade plan generator - tests/e2e/subnet-claim: new integration tests exercising claim/renew/drain/rollback path

Compatibility & migration notes: - Default behavior is unchanged; operators must opt-in by enabling the subnet-claim module and setting installer + helm flags. - For existing installs we provide a compatibility script that converts static-subnet mappings to lease-enabled resources; script documented in README. - DNS proxies require customer approval for additional privatelink endpoints; documented minimal IAM & SG changes included.

Testing & CI: - Unit tests for lease reconciler and Terraform module plan validation. - E2E run in perf-canary with multi-AZ VPC (simulated) validated claim handoff under packet-loss. - CI pipeline updated: terraform fmt/validate, helm lint, go-test, e2e smoke job.

Risks & mitigations: - Race conditions during claim: lease TTL + jittered backoff + expander logic reduce collisions; we also added a circuit-breaker to abort if >3 rapid failures. - DNS propagation: staged TTL lowering + health-check gating prevents large-scale TTL churn. - Privatelink proxy performance: default proxy scaled to 2 replicas per AZ; we recommend testing with customer traffic and enabling autoscaler for heavy workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + docs - [x] Installer lease controller - [x] Helm chart + schema - [x] E2E tests - [x] Upgrade / rollback helper commands - [x] CI updated

Related: ENG-3049 (subnet ownership), ENG-3116 (control plane failover), SUP-8891 (customer report describing flapping during upgrade).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: overall looks good, but we need clearer invariants for lease expiry during cross-account peering — please add a short design note.
Sofia Chen: added design notes in docs/private-installer/subnet-claims.md and clarified TTL behavior; also adjusted the retry loop to use exponential backoff with jitter.
Maya Patel: found a potential SG hole in privatelink-proxy default policy, requested tightening to restrict to controlplane CIDRs.
Sofia Chen: tightened SG rules and added helm values to override allowed CIDR ranges; pushed fix in commit f5a1d00.
Liam O'Connor: tested e2e in perf-canary; observed one transient DNS flapping during test run 3, added health-check gating to mitigate. Approving after fixes.
notes_for_ops: To enable: 1) deploy terraform/modules/subnet-claim into target account; 2) flip installer flag `subnetClaim.enabled=true`; 3) optionally deploy helm/privatelink-proxy with values `proxy.enabled=true` and set allowedCidrs; 4) run scripts/compat/convert-static-to-lease.sh if migrating existing stacks. For rollback, run `installer rollback-subnet-claim --dry-run` then without --dry-run to revert claims. Ensure Route53 record TTLs are restored after the maintenance window.
qa_summary: Unit tests: 86 passing; Integration: e2e-subnet-claim passed in 3/3 perf-canary runs after fixes. CI smoke job validated terraform plan output on a staging account. Manual verification steps documented in PR and docs/private-installer/subnet-claims.md.
